label: late-episode within-decile decay of z; higher at D2 after choosing a1
terms: (ep_trial >= 90) * (ep_trial - 94.5) * (phase == D2) ;; (ep_trial >= 90) * (ep_trial - 94.5) * (phase != D2) ;; (ep_trial >= 80) * (ep_trial < 90) * (ep_trial - 84.5) * (phase == D2) ;; (ep_trial >= 80) * (ep_trial < 90) * (ep_trial - 84.5) * (phase != D2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (1 + (ep_trial >= 70) * 2) ;; (phase == D2) * choice * (ep_trial >= 70)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 46 is near 1 (D1 ~0.98, GO ~0.997, D2 ~0.9) for most of the episode and collapses over the last ~20 trials (D2 first, then D1/GO in the last decile); the decile timing baseline already explains R^2 0.92. Most of the remaining variance is a finer-grained timing effect: a steady within-decile decline in trials 80-89 (mainly D2) and 90-99 (mainly D1/GO), captured by linear ep_trial slopes. The behavioural part is small: at D2, z is higher after the agent chose a1 (just made, observed) and, late in the episode, scales with the policy logit toward a1; this choice effect grows in trials 70+. Previous-trial outcome (e.g. lower at GO after unrewarded trials late in the episode), value and the hidden good state add <0.01. The behavioural terms alone give ~0.085 dev R^2 beyond timing (ceiling for additive cues = 0.14); with the within-decile slopes dev R^2 beyond timing = 0.56. Remaining errors are episode-to-episode differences in when the late decay starts, which none of the variables predict. No future variables used.
